note: `onPatch` deliberately declares NO `writes`, and the reason is the shape of what it emits rather than a gap in the row: it fires a NESTED PARTIAL — `{caps: {learn: {learnsAllowed: 3}}}` — that the router deep-merges into the draft, and the write-back engine assigns an argument to a knob whole. Writing that partial into `recipeItem` would REPLACE the draft with a single-key fragment and blank the card that raised it. So the toggles, steppers and typeaheads log their patch and the `recipeItem` knob is the honest route. The two `role="listbox"` typeaheads are why issue 1458 recorded this file at all: they have no trigger and no closed state, so they are comboboxes rather than a `SearchablePopover`, and this plinth is where that can be seen instead of taken on trust — type into one and the suggestion list hangs off the input.

note: PLAYER-WINDOW rooted, because it renders inside `ActorSelectTopBar`'s right slot in the crafting window. Its one prop is a services bag, so the row drives `services.craftingSources` as data — `sources`, `available` and `selectedSourceIds` — and the store's `remove` and `toggle` METHODS are absent, because no knob type carries a function. Every read is optional-chained, so the specimen mounts and draws correctly and the two write actions are inert: the plus button still opens the popover (that is component state, not store state), the option rows still report their selection, and clicking one changes nothing. That inertness is itself the point of the register entry — issue 1458's surviving disqualifier is that this is a MULTI-SELECT checklist whose panel stays open across choices, with `aria-selected` true on every chosen actor at once, against a primitive that has one `value` and closes on choose.
